title: Paying a Past-Due Customer-Funded Draw on a Reconstruction Contract
content:
A customer whose customer-funded draw on a Reconstruction contract has gone past due may bring it current with a payment through the company's secure payment channel.

## Scope

For the customer's payment toward the contract's most recently requested customer-funded draw, the one with the highest draw number among the customer-funded draws, once that draw is past due and every earlier customer-funded draw of the contract is paid in full, and only for that payment, the amount is worked out under the past-due payment rules, and the payment names that one draw and is posted in full to the contract. Every other payment names the one draw it pays and is posted in full to the contract, as the base payment rule states.

## Suspension and resumption

When a customer-funded draw stays unpaid for more than the tier's stop-work days after its due date, work is suspended, a Texas customer-funded draw that has everything but its statutory retention paid not being unpaid until the Texas statutory retention days after the substantial completion date have passed. For a draw paid by the payment these rules price, the draw counts as paid in full once that payment is posted, or at once when the payment works out to less than half a cent and none is taken, because the amounts that payment leaves unpaid on the draw are not due; work then resumes, and the tier's remobilization fee is booked once for that resumption. For every other draw, when the draw is paid in full, which on a Texas property until the Texas statutory retention days after the substantial completion date have passed is once everything but its statutory retention is paid, work resumes and the tier's remobilization fee is booked once for that resumption.

## The payment

The payment is the customer's own act: the customer pays through the company's secure payment channel by debit card, ACH, check or wire, and staff never take card or account numbers.

The amount of a payment that brings a past-due draw current is worked out only after the records carry the overdue draw charge owed on that draw for each calendar month fee period that is owed; a fee period owes no overdue draw charge, and no charge is recorded for it, when the charge worked out for it comes to less than half a cent.

The past-due payment is fixed only after no deductive change order proposal remains on the contract awaiting the customer's signature; a deductive proposal whose credit worked out under the deductive change order signature rule is nothing is not counted, because it cannot be written.

A payment that works out to less than half a cent is not taken: no payment is posted, and the draw counts as paid in full at once, because nothing on it is due.

## Invocation: `pay_past_due_draw_ec4ba96a`

`pay_past_due_draw_ec4ba96a` is a customer-owned tool: the agent unlocks it and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it through the company's secure payment channel. One call records one draw payment, dated today, naming the draw, the tender used and the amount, issues a confirmation number for it, and lowers the contract balance by the amount paid. Afterwards the payment appears among the contract's payments with its confirmation number and the contract balance is lower by the payment.

### Parameters

- `rebuild_contract_id` — the reference number of the customer's Reconstruction contract, as given to the customer by the representative from the contract lookup.
- `rebuild_draw_id` — the reference number of the draw the payment pays, as given to the customer by the representative from the draw lookup for that contract.
- `payment_method` — the tender used, exactly one of: `debit_card` (paid with the customer's debit card); `ach` (an electronic transfer from the customer's bank account); `check` (a paper check); `wire` (a bank wire transfer); `mortgagee_check` (a check issued by the mortgagee from its loss-draft account).
- `amount` — the amount paid in US dollars, a number with exactly 2 decimal places; any further digits are rounded to the cent, half up.

### Return

A one-line confirmation naming the payment confirmation number (a text id beginning "rpy_"), the draw reference, the tender, the amount paid in US dollars with 2 decimals and the new contract balance in US dollars with 2 decimals. The presence of the confirmation number means the payment was recorded.
